hectospec.title: MMT / Hectospec (300-fiber bench spectrograph, plane reflection gratings, catadioptric camera)
hectospec.recommended_preset: 270 gpm grating (blaze 5200 A per the manuals and MMTO; 'blazed at 5000 A' in F05), first order, set up for H-alpha: angle of incidence 22.83 deg, diffraction angle 12.17 deg on the camera side (fixed 35 deg camera-collimator angle; the published angles obey sin(alpha) - sin(beta) = m g lambda, see Notes), 250 um / 1.5" fiber at f/5.3, spherical collimator mirror (f ~1374 mm DERIVED from the Zemax radius; beam 259 mm), catadioptric camera 397 mm, two E2V 42-90 CCDs with 4608 px x 13.5 um along dispersion. Validate against: 1.21 A/px (manual, MMTO) or 1.2 A/px (F05); 6.2 A FWHM (F05) or 5.8-5.0 A measured at 4500/7000 A (manual); coverage 4488-8664 A over the nominal 3400 px (manual table) and 5770 A over the full chip (manual; MMTO 3650-9200 A); R ~1000-2000 (F05). The grating equation reproduces the manual's angles to 1 A and the A/px to 2% (DERIVED, Notes). The 600 gpm grating (AOI 29.41 deg, 0.55 A/px, 2.2-1.9 A FWHM, R up to ~3700) is fully tabulated as the alternative.

notes: Pupil slicing and the app (DERIVED reasoning): in PRV/NS-PRV each of the 7 fibres sees the whole 0.8" star image through ONE 8.4 m segment (100 um at f/3 on 8.4 m = 0.82"), and each fibre's f/8 output fills the full 300 mm beam. The spectrum of each slice is therefore that of an 8.4 m telescope with a 0.8" fibre; the 7 slices are stacked along the slit and add signal. Model it as D = 8.4 m with a 0.8" fibre (or D = 25.4 m with a 0.265" fibre = GC14D's '0.26" (7x)'); multiply collected flux by 7 (pupil area of all segments).

R validation caveat (DERIVED): with f_cam,eff = 675 mm and tan(theta_B) = 4.0, a Littrow R computed with LSF FWHM = geometric fibre-image width gives 72,000 (PRV, 75 um), 24,000 (MR, 225 um), 16,000 (HT, 337.5 um) -- vs published 108k/35k/19k. The published PRV and MR values imply FWHM = 0.67-0.69 x the image diameter (GC14D Table 5: FWHM 3.65 x 15 um = 54.8 um vs an 83 um geometric image, ratio 0.66). A uniformly lit disk projected on the dispersion axis has FWHM = 0.866 x D (R = 83k PRV). Hectochelle's paper quotes a 1.46 'boost' for the same effect.

White pupil mapping: the app's collimator = M1 (2400 mm, 300 mm beam, f/8); camera = 675 mm effective on the 300 mm beam (physical 450 mm on the 200 mm beam after the 1.5x pupil transfer). The cross-disperser sits in the 200 mm beam, so its angular dispersion is multiplied by 450 mm (not 675 mm) at the detector.

Design history: 2012 concept (GC12) -> 2014 PDR (GC14D/GC14O; PDR held April 2015 per GC16O) -> 2016 post-PDR re-optimisation (GC16D/GC16O) -> 2018 pre-CDR (GC18D/GC18O) -> 2023 G@M plan (GCM23) -> 2024-2025 assembly/testing (GC24, GC25). Values in the preset are 2016-2018.

Glass: not needed for the recommended red-arm preset (pure VPH grating). A blue-arm preset would need fused silica for the two grism prisms (Malitson 1965 coefficients are in round 1, key MAL65) plus the unpublished prism orientation.
